【原视频简介】
Kway Chap has always been one of my favourite Singaporean hawker classics, and this time I’m making it from scratch at home! 🇸🇬

I first made Kway Chap when we were living in Shanghai during COVID, when I couldn’t come home to Singapore and started recreating the dishes I missed. This is my tried-and-tested version, now made for a Kway Chap dinner with friends!

In this Slow Day, I’ll show you how I make the braising liquid, prepare the pork belly and pre-cooked large intestines, make the chilli sauce, and prepare the two aromatic toppings that I think make Kway Chap extra special — crispy garlic and fried shallots with their infused oils. 

I’ve also shared a few little tips along the way, including my shortcut for the large intestines and how I make my hard-boiled eggs. And yes… there’s no small intestine because I don’t eat it! 🤣

📖 Full Kway Chap recipe: https://asingaporeanmum.com/2026/08/29/homemade-kway-chap/

Come along for more slow days, home cooking and little moments from our everyday lives. 🌿
